mem.t: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.

lessons.title: Goodness Comes from God
lessons.theme: Goodness is not the polish of a good person but the overflow of God's nature

v: Oh taste and see that the LORD is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.
Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.

lessons.still: Sit comfortably with your open hands resting on your knees, as if receiving a gift. Slowly count your blessings: today's breath, the sunlight, your food, the people around you; all of it has come down from the Father of lights. Softly say, “Lord, you are good.”
teach: Whether well water tastes sweet doesn't depend on the bucket but on the source. We often think of “goodness” as a personal quality: being good-tempered, helpful, never harming anyone. But Jesus said, “No one is good except one: God.” Human goodness cut off from God is like a bucket cut off from its spring; before long it runs dry.

The psalmist invites us to “taste and see that the Lord is good,” because God's goodness is not a theory but something we can experience. James says every good and perfect gift is “from above,” from the Father “with whom can be no variation, nor turning shadow.” The sun sets, the moon waxes and wanes, human hearts change; only God's goodness never changes.

So the goodness the Spirit produces is not me trying hard to become a good person; it is the God who is good living in me, and his goodness flowing out through me. The mindset shift: from “I must be a good person” to “I must abide in the good God.” Get the source right, and the water will be sweet.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-ruled goodness usually comes with self-promotion: “I'm a good person.” Self-emptied goodness gives the glory to the source: “It is God's goodness in me.” Let Jesus reign and let Jesus receive all the glory, including the glory for our good deeds.
q: Who is God? — “With whom can be no variation, nor turning shadow.” What qualities of God's goodness do you see here?
Who am I? — Does your “goodness” come from God, or do you prop it up by your own effort?
How shall I respond? — How will you “taste and see that the Lord is good” today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus “went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him” (Acts 10:38). His good deeds were not done to build a reputation; they were the Father's goodness flowing naturally through him. He said that by himself he could do nothing, but only what he saw the Father doing.
lessons.pray: Good and gracious God, thank you for every good gift you have given me. I confess that there is no goodness in me; whatever good there is comes from you. Be the source of my life, and let your goodness flow out of me, so that people see you and not me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down five good gifts you have received from God today
For one of my 2s: tell them one good thing God has given them
After doing a good deed, pray silently: “Glory to the God who is good.”
lessons.noon: “Oh taste and see that the LORD is good.” — Lord, right now let me taste your goodness.

lessons.title: Don't Grow Weary in Doing Good
lessons.theme: Sow to the Spirit, and in due season there will be a harvest

v: For he who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption. But he who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life.
Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.
So then, as we have opportunity, let’s do what is good toward all men, and especially toward those who are of the household of the faith.

lessons.still: Imagine you are a farmer holding a handful of seed. Recall, one by one, the good things you have done lately that have brought no return, and place them in the Lord's hand like seed being sown, saying, “Lord, the time of harvest is yours.” Then breathe quietly, and let go of the anxious need to see results right away.
teach: A farmer who sows his seed doesn't dig up the soil the next day to see whether it has sprouted. While the seed is hidden underground, it is putting down roots. Doing good is like that: we give, and the other person doesn't say thank you, nothing changes, and we may even be misunderstood. At such times the greatest temptation is not to do evil but to “grow weary”: forget it, why bother?

Paul says there are two ways of sowing: sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit. If we do good to win people's praise, we are sowing to the flesh, and when the applause stops we lose heart. If we do good by following the Spirit, we don't look at people's response but at God's timing. “In due season”: the harvest timetable is in God's hands, not ours.

“As we have opportunity, let us do good to all”: doing good is not an occasional burst of enthusiasm but a way of life. We grow weary usually because our focus has drifted to results or to other people. Turn the focus back to Jesus: I do good because he was good to me first, and he will never forget a single seed sown for his name.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Keep your focus on Jesus, not on yourself, not on others, not on circumstances. Calculate the returns with your head and you will be full of worry; live from the heart by the Spirit and your heart will be glad. Shift your perspective from the temporary to the eternal: the harvest you cannot see today will not lose a single grain in eternity.
q: Who is God? — “We will reap in due season.” How do you trust the God who holds the seasons?
Who am I? — In which good work have you already begun to lose heart?
How shall I respond? — Where will you keep on “sowing to the Spirit” today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus spent his life doing good, and in return he was rejected, betrayed and crucified. From a human point of view it was the greatest “waste” of all; from God's point of view it was the greatest harvest. “For the joy that was set before him he endured the cross, despising its shame.” A grain of wheat fell into the ground and produced many seeds.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that after doing good for a long time I grow tired, and I long to be noticed. Renew my resolve, so that I no longer sow for people's applause but sow to the Spirit. I place the time of harvest in your hands; give me strength not to lose heart. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Keep on with one good work you nearly gave up on
For one of my 2s: keep up a kind gesture toward them without expecting anything in return
Write “The time of harvest is in God's hands” and put it where you will often see it
lessons.noon: “Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.” — Lord, right now strengthen my heart.

lessons.title: The Good Works of Dorcas
lessons.theme: The good works God prepared are shown through ordinary hands

v: Peter got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the tunics and other garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.

lessons.still: Look at your hands. Today they may type on a keyboard, cook a meal, hold a child or sweep the floor. Lift them up and offer them to the Lord: “Lord, these hands are yours; please use them.” Be silent for a moment, and ask the Lord to show you one need around you.
teach: Dorcas never preached a sermon or performed a miracle. Scripture records only that she was “full of good works and acts of mercy”. When she died, the widows gathered around Peter weeping, and what they held in their hands was not her sermons but the tunics and garments she had sewn herself. Every stitch was her testimony left behind on earth.

Paul says, “We are his workmanship.” The word carries the sense of a masterpiece, a work of art. God has re-created us in Christ “for good works”, and these good works are ones “which God prepared beforehand” for us. It is like a road already laid down; we simply obey and walk on it. Good works are not something we dream up to prove ourselves; they are what God has placed on our path ahead of time.

We often think only big things count as serving, but Dorcas's needle and thread tell us that in God's eyes nothing is small. The fruit of goodness often grows in the most ordinary places: a meal, a garment, a phone call. The mindset shift: not “I must do something remarkable,” but “What good work has God prepared for me today?”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied person needs no stage, because they do not live for their own name. Dorcas's good works let the widows see God's love, and later many came to believe in the Lord because of what happened. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: a good life naturally builds relationships, and relationships naturally become bridges for the gospel.
q: Who is God? — God has “prepared” good works for you. What kind of God does this show you?
Who am I? — What ordinary things do you have in your hands that could become God's “needle and thread”?
How shall I respond? — What good work has God placed on your path today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus took a boy's five loaves and two fish, gave thanks, broke them and handed them to the disciples, and five thousand were fed. He did not despise a small lunch. He also stooped to wash his disciples' feet: the Lord of the universe displayed God's goodness with a towel and a basin of water.
lessons.pray: Lord my Creator, thank you for calling me your workmanship and for preparing good works for me to do. Open my eyes to see the people you have placed on my path, and use my ordinary hands, as you used Dorcas's, to pass on your love stitch by stitch. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Prepare a small, practical help for someone in need around you
For one of my 2s: do one concrete act of service, such as bringing a meal or writing a card
In the evening, reflect: “Did I do the good work God prepared for me today?”
lessons.noon: “For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works” — Lord, right now let me see the good work you have prepared.

lessons.title: Overcoming Evil with Good
lessons.theme: Evil cannot be defeated by evil, only overcome by good

v: Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
not rendering evil for evil or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.

lessons.still: Think of someone who has hurt you and made you want to hit back. Don't suppress your feelings; tell the Lord honestly, “Lord, I am hurt.” Then breathe deeply, lay your thoughts of revenge like stones at the foot of the cross, and ask the Lord to give you a heart that blesses.
teach: Fight fire with fire and the blaze only grows; only water puts it out. When we are treated badly, our instinct is to repay evil with evil: you're cold to me, so I'll be cold to you; you say one thing to me, I'll say two back. The evil snowballs and both sides lose. This is exactly how pride provokes pride.

Paul says, “Don't be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” Repaying evil with evil looks like fighting back, but in fact it means evil has won: it has succeeded in turning me into an evildoer too. Peter goes further: “but instead blessing,” because “you were called to this.” Blessing our enemies is not weakness; it is a heavenly victory.

Overcoming evil with good does not mean swallowing our anger and pretending nothing happened; it means refusing to let evil decide how I respond. I can set boundaries and speak the truth, yet without holding a grudge or taking revenge, leaving vengeance to God. The key is: who is reigning right now? If self is on the throne, I will want to settle the score; if Jesus is on the throne, I can bless the other person.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility overcomes pride; the self-emptied life overcomes Satan. What Satan wants most is to get us repaying evil for evil, trapped in the cycle of the self-ruled life. Humility inspires humility, and both sides win. Overcoming evil with good is exactly how the vicious cycle is broken and God's kingdom system is built.
q: Who is God? — God was good to us while we were still his enemies. What does this teach you about him?
Who am I? — Is there a debt in your heart that you want to “collect”?
How shall I respond? — What specific good can you return for an evil today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was insulted, he did not answer back; as he was being crucified, he prayed for those who nailed him there: “Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.” The cross looked like the triumph of evil, but it was in fact the ultimate victory of good. He absorbed all evil with love, and overcame it all.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, on the cross you overcame evil with good. I confess that I often want to repay evil with evil and settle the score. Today I hand my right to vengeance over to you. Keep me from being overcome by evil, and enable me instead to bless those who have hurt me. Reign in my heart. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray a prayer of blessing for someone who has hurt you
For one of my 2s: when there's friction, hold back from hitting back and say something kind instead
When you are offended today, pray silently: “Don't be overcome by evil.”
lessons.noon: “Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” — Lord, right now help me respond with good.

lessons.title: Doing Good to My 2
lessons.theme: Let good works be a light that shines on those around us

v: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
But don’t forget to be doing good and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

lessons.still: In your heart, list three of “my 2s”: family, colleagues, neighbours or brothers and sisters in Christ. Pause quietly over each name, asking the Lord to show you what they need right now, and how you can be a blessing to them.
teach: A lamp doesn't need to announce loudly, “I'm shining!” Once it is lit, the room is simply filled with light. This week we have seen that the source of goodness is God (Day 1), that we must not grow weary in doing good (Day 2), that we do the good God has prepared in ordinary ways (Day 3), and that we overcome evil with good (Day 4). Today we bring goodness to the people closest to us: our 2s.

Jesus said to let people “see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.” Notice the direction of the glory: it goes not to the one doing good but to the Father in heaven. Hebrews says doing good and sharing are sacrifices that please God; our good deeds are themselves an act of worship offered to God.

Doing good to “my 2s” is hardest, because they know us best and rub up against us most often. But for that very reason, our goodness is most real in front of them. Next week we will learn “faithfulness”, and faithfulness is exactly the strength that makes goodness last: not being good to people now and then, but being reliably good to them over the long haul.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The practice of 920: every person I am in relationship with is my 2; I live out the 0 of the self-emptied life; and the 9, the fruit of the Spirit, grows. Goodness is not done to be seen but so that the Father is glorified. Letting Jesus receive all the glory is the final direction of every good deed.
q: Who is God? — God is pleased with the sacrifice of doing good. What does this show you about what God values?
Who am I? — In the eyes of your 2s, are you a steady lamp or one that flickers on and off?
How shall I respond? — This week, toward which 2 will you keep doing one good thing?
lessons.jesus: Jesus was most patient in doing good to his closest disciples: when Peter was weak, he prayed for Peter; when Thomas doubted, he held out his hands; when the disciples argued about who was the greatest, he washed their feet. His light was not a distant searchlight but a lamp close at hand, lighting up the people beside him day after day.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for making me the light of the world. I place my 2s in your hands one by one. Help me show them your goodness, not for my own name but only for your glory. May they see not me, but you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: do one concrete good deed for them, and don't mention it
Write a one-line prayer for each of three 2s, and pray for them every day for a week
Tomorrow (Saturday), share with a spiritual companion how you did good this week
lessons.noon: “That they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.” — Lord, right now let my light shine out your glory.
